title: Changing sickness symptom expectations: Effects on objective and subjective symptom dynamics in an experimental model of inflammation-induced sickness
summary:
"Sickness Behavior" or sickness symptoms refers to a range of nonspecific, immune-mediated symptoms such as fever, fatigue, increased pain sensitivity, as well as behavioral and mood changes, including anxiety, depression, and social withdrawal. These sickness symptoms arise from the activation of the immune system, particularly through pro-inflammatory cytokines that reach the brain. In the case of an acute inflammation or infection, the sickness symptoms provide a protective function, whereas in chronic inflammation, they become an additional burden that significantly impacts the quality of life of the affected individuals and limits the tolerance and adherence to immunomodulatory treatments.

Previous studies have shown that negative expectations as well as anxierty regarding the occurrence and intensity of undesirable symptoms and side effects influence the perception of symptoms, responses to treatments, and adherence to immune-directed therapies. This highlights the need for novel approaches and improved doctor-patient communication in clinical practice to reduce negative expectations, while fostering positive expectations.

A pilot study has demonstrated that the expectations of participants play a role in how effectively an anti-inflammatory drug alleviates inflammation symptoms. Building on this, the current experimental study additionally investigates the effects of doctor-patient communication on dynamic changes in expectations and the perception of immune-mediated sickness symptoms in healthy participants.

interventions.name: Single injection of endotoxin (E. coli, 0113:H10; i.v., 0.8 ng/kg body weight) to induce a systemic inflammatory response; single administration of an anti-inflammatory drug (Ibuprofen, oral, 400 mg), verbal manipulation of treatment expectations (augmented).

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
Healthy male and female participants aged 18 to 50 years.
Exclusion criteria:
Acute or chronic physical illnesses (e.g., gastrointestinal diseases, liver and kidney diseases, cardiovascular diseases, diabetes mellitus, obesity). Pathological laboratory values (e.g., CRP). Regular use of medications (except for oral contraception). Contraindications for ibuprofen. Indications of psychiatric disorders according to DSM-V criteria based on validated screening instruments (particularly depression and anxiety disorders). MRI-specific exclusion criteria (anxiety disorders, particularly claustrophobia, metallic implants, metal-containing tattoos, etc.). Additional exclusion criteria for female participants: pregnancy or breastfeeding.
